m: The {Baker} stands on the {Rooftop} of the {Spa} and whips open a pair of *curtains*. Behind them sit **eight** octopuses in fluffy bathrobes, each waving **eight** arms, and each arm holding a cupcake. The baker counts on his fingers: eight times eight, sixty-four cupcakes, and he still has to make the tea.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Lagoon}'s lighthouse, the {Gardener} slams a giant marrow onto a *workbench*, and a *strong arm* hammers a gold medal onto it. Biggest vegetable in history! What an **achievement**! Fish leap out of the water to applaud, and the marrow is so proud of its **achievement** that it demands a statue.

On the {Front Step} of the {Spa}, the {Magician} meets a *horse* with a huge *mouth* that turns everything into a **yes-no question**. Is it sunny, ma? Am I a horse, ma? Is this a spa, ma? The magician can only nod or shake his head, and after the hundredth **yes-no question** his top hat falls off.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Tower}, the {Baker} **wraps** a *parcel* in brown paper, then **wraps** the paper in more paper, then wraps the string, the scissors and the pigeon watching him. By sunset the whole tower is **wrapped** up like a birthday present, with the baker somewhere inside.

The {Pirate} kicks open the {Trapdoor} of the {Yen Exchange} and starts shaving a log into *wood slices*, each one a **thin piece** you can see straight through. He hands them out as treasure maps. The bankers hold every **thin piece** up to the light, but each map only shows another pirate slicing wood.

In the {Basement} of the {Beehive}, the {Sheriff} finds a dusty *historian* reading out the hive's entire **history**: the Great Honey Flood, the War of the Wasps, the year the queen sneezed. He has been talking for nine hundred years. The sheriff dozes off and wakes up as a footnote in **history** himself.

In a {Basement} under the {Lake}, the {Wizard} **entrusts** his last *wilting stalk* of magic wheat to a frog. Keep it safe, he whispers. The frog guards it day and night, watering it, singing to it, fending off herons with a twig. By spring the stalk is a golden field, and the wizard **entrusts** the frog with his wand too.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Pool}, the {Hunter} blows a *whistle* **at** everything: **at** the swimmers, **at** the clouds, at a passing helicopter. Each blast blows its target backwards, so swimmers shoot out of the water and clouds wobble. Finally he blows it at himself and tumbles off the roof into the deep end.

The {Chef} tiptoes up the {Staircase} of the {Spa} at *sunrise* with a clipboard and **checks** every *tree* in the garden: leaves, branches, birds' nests. Then she **checks** the bathtubs, the towels and the eyebrows of every sleepy guest. The manager asks what she is looking for. She checks her clipboard: breakfast.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Boxing Ring}, the {Cheerleader} loads a *cart* with feathers, bubbles and dandelion fluff. It is so **light** that it floats off the roof like a balloon, with her clinging to the handle. She sails over the city, **light** as air, waving her pom-poms at astonished pigeons.

The {Yogi} pops out of a {Trapdoor} on the {Beach} and watches a *lizard* do every impossible yoga pose: a handstand on one claw, a pretzel, a backflip into a coconut. It looks so **easy**! He tries. He ties himself into a sailor's knot, and the lizard yawns: **easy** for some.

In the {Basement} of the {Tower}, the {Zookeeper} is woken at four in the morning by an *early bird* tapping on his forehead. It is far too **early**! He hides under the pillow, but the bird fetches a trumpet, a rooster and a marching band. By dawn the whole tower is up very **early**, eating cornflakes in the dark.

The {Tsar} climbs a vine {Staircase} in the {Jungle} and finds an old bamboo *steamer* with a note inside: Here **once** lived a dumpling. He lifts the lid, and a cloud of steam acts out the tale of the dumpling who **once** ruled the jungle, before a monkey ate it. The tsar takes off his hat in respect.

The {Chef} stomps down the {Staircase} into the {Pool} with a shovel, because a whole *hillside* of *leftovers* has slid into the water: cold noodles, soggy chips, one lonely sprout. She **removes** it scoop by scoop, flinging it over the fence. The swimmers cheer, until she **removes** them too, by mistake.

The {Ninja} creeps down the {Staircase} into the {Lagoon} and finds an underwater *farm*: sea cows grazing, crabs ploughing, octopuses milking clams. He swaps his sword for a pitchfork and takes up **farming**. By autumn he is harvesting seaweed in perfect silence, the stealthiest **farming** the lagoon has ever seen.

In the {Basement} of the {Tower}, the {Jockey} **looks for** his lost horse with a *halberd*, poking behind barrels and under rugs. A *helping hand* joins in, then the guards, then the cook. Everybody **looks for** the horse for hours, while the horse sits upstairs on the throne, nibbling the crown.

On the {Rooftop} of a shack in the {Swamp}, the {Jockey} watches a *strongman* **adorn** himself in a silky *robe* covered in sequins, frogs and fairy lights. Not enough! he roars, and **adorns** the robe with a chandelier and a live heron. He glitters so brightly that the swamp's fireflies go home in shame.

In the {Basement} of an old *shed* in the {Swamp}, the {Gardener} pushes on a wall and it slides back, and back, and back. The shed grows **wider** and **wider** until it holds a football pitch, three ponds and a herd of puzzled cows. The gardener still cannot find his rake in a room so **wide**.

In the {Basement} of the {Yen Exchange}, the {Shepherd} whips a cloth off a glass *showcase* to **reveal** its treasure: a single golden sheep. Gasps! He whips off another cloth to **reveal** another, and another, until his whole flock is **revealed**, sparkling, and the bankers start bidding for them.

On the {Front Step} of the {Spa}, the {Baker} meets a *python* whose smiling *mouth* tacks a soft **suggestion particle** onto everything: Let's take a bath, ba. Let's share a bun, ba. The baker cannot refuse such polite **suggestions**, so soon they are both in a bubble bath, eating buns, ba.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Spa}, the {Ghost} meets an *auntie* who sticks a cosy **name prefix** onto everyone: A-Ghostie, A-Towel, A-Steamy. She puts the **name prefix** on the masseur, the sauna and even the moon. The ghost is so flattered to be A-Ghostie that he stays for tea and cucumber slices.

In a {Basement} under the {Beach}, the {Lifeguard} finds a *child* who has grown a *tree* in a sand bucket. It drips with purple **plums** the size of beach balls. The child hurls them like dodgeballs, and the lifeguard blows her whistle, catches a **plum** and eats it in one juicy slurp.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Cat Café}, the {Baker} squeezes an icing bag to **mark** everything: an X on the *tree*, a star on the *altar*, a smiley face on each cat. The cats are furious and **mark** him back with muddy paw prints, until he looks like a spotty dog.

On the {Staircase} of the {Mansion}, the {Tailor} sits by a crackling *blaze* and **talks** with a *small speech bubble* that talks back. They **talk** about buttons, then hems, then the meaning of life. The talk gets so heated that the bubble catches fire, and they carry on chatting through the smoke.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Beehive}, the {Chef} serves dinner to a *beggar* with an enormous *mouth*. He **eats** the soup, the bread, the table and the tablecloth. Still hungry, he **eats** the chef's hat and three honeycombs, then politely asks what is for pudding.

On the {Staircase} of the {Pool}, the {Tailor} paints a **picture** of a *winter coat* on a garden *fence*. It looks so real that the shivering swimmers try to put it on. He adds a scarf, then a mug of cocoa, until the fence is one huge **picture** of a cosy ski lodge, and everyone climbs inside.

The {Ninja} creeps up through the {Trapdoor} of the {Yen Exchange} and, instead of stealing anything, **reads aloud** a love poem to the giant *clock* with all his *heart*. The traders stop shouting to listen. He **reads aloud** a second poem, even louder, and the clock blushes and chimes thirteen.

The {Lifeguard} opens a {Trapdoor} in the {Youth Hostel}, and a pair of giant *dice* tumbles out. Every throw lands on **six**. Six! Six! Six! The backpackers bet their socks, their snacks, their bunks. By midnight the lifeguard owns **six** beds, **six** sandwiches and six very smelly socks.

In the {Basement} of the {Inn}, the {Yogi} hooks a giant *bow* onto a *pole* and **pulls** back the string, slowly, breathing deeply. He **pulls** so far that the pole bends, the barrels roll and the innkeeper is dragged in by his apron. Then he lets go, and the whole cellar is fired into the garden.

The {Lifeguard} opens a {Trapdoor} on the {Beach}, and a *strong arm* hauls her up a *cliff* for the **experience** of a lifetime: bungee jumping, eagle wrestling, a ride on a cloud. She comes back down with frizzy hair and a sunburnt nose, having **experienced** everything except a quiet afternoon.

In the {Basement} of the {Boathouse}, the {Sheriff} finds a giant stone *head* wearing a captain's hat. The **head** opens its eyes and starts barking orders: row left, row right, polish my nose. The sheriff salutes, and the head, being the **head** of the boathouse, promotes him to chief oar.

On the {Rooftop} of a pier café on the {Beach}, the {Yogi} finds an *open crate* full of **medicine** and an *arrow* pointing at a sunburnt walrus. He spoons the **medicine** into its mouth. The walrus turns from lobster red back to grey, sings a little opera, and asks for a second spoonful.

On the {Staircase} of the {Museum}, the {Juggler} trips over a *lying man* who has set up his **office** right there: desk, phone and filing cabinet balanced on his tummy. People queue on the steps to get forms stamped. The juggler joins the queue, and by lunch he has a job in the **office**, juggling paperwork.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Pool}, the {Tailor} is sewing quietly when a *dog* bursts out of a *cave* in the chimney with a **sudden** bark. He jumps so high that his needle shoots into the clouds. Then, all of a **sudden**, the dog sneezes, and the tailor tumbles into the deep end.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Swan Pond}'s tearoom, the {Jockey} turns a magic *spindle* that spins a **special** thread, softer than swan feathers. He weaves a **special** saddle for one very **special** swan, and the next morning that swan wins every race on the pond, with the jockey bouncing on its back.

The {Firefighter} opens a {Trapdoor} on a jetty in the {Lake}, and a crab with a *dollar sign* painted on its *shell* scuttles out with a bill. Rescuing a cat **costs** ten shells, it snaps. Sitting on the jetty **costs** five. Breathing costs one. By the time she leaves, the crab owns her helmet.

The {Hunter} pops through the {Trapdoor} at the top of the {Tower}, and a giant *mouth* blows out a *puff of breath* shaped like a **number**: seven. Then thirty-two. Then a million. The **numbers** drift over the city like clouds, and everyone below jumps up and shouts bingo.

In the {Basement} of the {Inn}, the {Juggler} balances a *ruler* on his nose and juggles *two sparks* on top, pushing himself **to the utmost**. Sweat drips, the sparks fizz, the innkeeper holds his breath. Then he adds a teapot, straining **to the utmost**, and everything stays up until he sneezes.

The {Lifeguard} drops through a {Trapdoor} into the {Boxing Ring} with a bag of *spare parts*. Every time a boxer is knocked down, she bolts on **another** arm, **another** glove, another nose. By the last round one boxer has eight arms and wins by tickling, and the loser demands **another** match.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Boathouse}, the {Jockey} rides a toy horse round a tiny *circuit*, one lap per day. Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday: after seven laps a whole **week** has gone by and his beard has grown. He keeps going, lap after lap, and the rowers mark each **week** with a chalk tally on his back.

The {Juggler} pops through a {Trapdoor} in the {Cat Café} and finds two cats sitting with *crossed legs* on a *cart*, **comparing** whiskers with a ruler. Then they **compare** tails, purrs and the number of naps they took today. The juggler measures himself too, and the cats agree he **compares** poorly: no whiskers at all.

The {Jockey} rises through a {Trapdoor} in the middle of the {Pool}, balancing a lit *candle* on his helmet while *water drops* splash all around him. He must **focus**. A beach ball bounces off his nose. He keeps his **focus**. A whale surfaces right beside him. He does not blink, and the flame never flickers.

In the {Basement} of the {Museum}, the {Yogi} finds a *speaker* blasting out a *small speech bubble* in a new **language** every second: Welsh, Swahili, dolphin, toaster. The mummies sit up and start chatting in a **language** nobody has spoken for four thousand years, mostly complaining about the dust.

In the {Basement} of the {Inn}, the {Juggler} meets a *standing person* who juggles with **only** a *right hand*. Just one hand, and yet twelve plates, a cat and a bowling ball stay in the air. The juggler tries it with **only** his right hand and is promptly buried under a heap of plates.

In the {Basement} of the {Tower}, the {King} sits at a tiny desk, sweating over an *exam*. The jester **tests** him on everything: crown polishing, banquet maths, how to wave. The king fails, so the jester **tests** the throne instead, which passes with top marks and gets to wear the crown.

The {Lifeguard} steps on a {Trapdoor} in the {Warehouse} and **falls**, straight through the floor, past the *grass* roots, past the worms, landing with a splash on an underground *riverbank*. Boxes **fall** after her, then a forklift, then a very surprised warehouse manager.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Boxing Ring}, the {Cheerleader} rolls across a carpet of fuzzy *moss* and stands up completely **green**. Her pom-poms are green, her teeth are green, even her cheers sound **green**. The boxers think she is a cheering cabbage and offer her salad dressing.

The {Sailor} stumbles down the {Staircase} of the {Waiting Room}, and a *pilgrim* starts to **follow** him, step for step, out of the door and up a *hillside*. Then the patients **follow** the pilgrim, then the doctor, then a goat. At the top the sailor turns round to find the whole town behind him, and nobody knows where they are going.

In the {Basement} of the {Mint}, the {Shepherd} lines up his sheep at the start of a *road* painted on the floor. They race, and he must **choose** a *front runner* to win a golden coin. It is an eleven-way tie. He **chooses** all eleven, and the mint has to stamp eleven coins in a hurry.

The {Lifeguard} opens a {Trapdoor} in the {Yeti Cave} and blows her whistle: everyone **line up**! Yetis shuffle into a *lineup*, tallest to shortest, then hairiest to baldest. One keeps sneaking to the front, so she makes them **line up** again by shoe size, and that takes all winter.

In the {Basement} of the {Pool}, the {Wizard} trains a *warrior* in **martial** arts: kicks, chops, a flying somersault over the boiler. She is so good she can split a stack of floats with one finger. The wizard, deeply impressed, swaps his wand for a pair of nunchucks and signs up for **martial** arts classes.

On the {Staircase} down to the {Lagoon}, the {Hunter} sets up a *workbench* and dyes a reel of *silk thread* bright **red**. He wraps it round everything: the rocks, the boats, a startled flamingo. Soon the whole lagoon glows **red**, and even the fish start blushing.

In the {Basement} of the {Stadium}, the {Shepherd} finds a *weathervane* with a huge *mouth* that makes a **sound** every time it spins: moo, honk, foghorn, opera. The crowd upstairs goes silent to listen. Then the wind picks up, and the **sound** gets so loud that the goalposts start dancing.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Waiting Room}, the {Sailor} is cornered by a *mosquito* the size of a seagull. **Although** it is huge, it is very polite and asks permission before every bite. **Although** he says no, it waits patiently in the queue downstairs with everyone else, reading old magazines.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Waiting Room}, the {Tailor} watches a *sparrow* try to **push** a sofa off the edge with its beak. A *helping hand* joins in, and together they **push** the sofa, a piano and a sleeping patient over the gutter, where they all land neatly on a trampoline.

The {Sheriff} kicks open the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} and slaps *handcuffs* on a wasp, but its *strong arm* snaps them like spaghetti. Such **power**! The wasp flexes, lifts the hive and juggles three bears. The sheriff hands over his badge, because the wasp clearly has more **power** than he does.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Mansion}, the {Tsar} stumbles on a race between knobbly *ginseng* roots with tiny legs. Everybody **takes part**: the butler, the cook, the dog, a passing pigeon. The tsar cannot resist, hitches up his royal robe and **takes part** too, coming last behind a root.

On the {Rooftop} of a beach bar on the {Beach}, the {Shepherd} knits a giant net out of *lace*, **hoping** to catch a shooting star. He waits all night, **hoping** and hoping. At dawn a star finally drops in, tangled in the lace, and asks very politely to be put back.

In the {Basement} of the {Pool}, the {Gardener} digs up an *antique* rubber duck, cracked and furry with moss. It is **ancient**: carvings show pharaohs bathing with it. The duck opens one eye and quacks in an **ancient** language, demanding its bath at once.

The {Jockey} opens a {Trapdoor} on a raft in the {Lagoon}, and out climbs a *person*, then another *person*, then a third *person*, then hundreds more. Soon a whole **crowd** is squeezed onto the raft, cheering, waving flags and eating hot dogs. The raft sinks lower and lower, and the **crowd** goes for a swim.

The {Gardener} climbs out of the {Trapdoor} of the {Boathouse}, chops down a *tree* and uses a giant *hook* to swing the logs into place. He **constructs** a boat, then a bigger boat, then a floating castle with turrets. The ducks watch him **construct** a moat round it and ask where the drawbridge is.

On the {Staircase} of the {Hangar}, the {Firefighter} finds a single *door* standing in a chalk *square*. She opens it, and behind it unfolds a whole **house**: kitchen, bedrooms, a cat in the window. She steps in, the door clicks shut, and now the **house** lives inside the hangar, with planes parking in its garden.

The {Baker} pops up through the {Trapdoor} of the {Mansion} with a giant bread knife and saws every guest's dinner in *half*. Then he cuts the table in **half**, the piano, the chandelier. When the duchess complains, he slices her hat in **half** too, and she storms off looking like a boiled egg.

On the icy {Staircase} of the {Yeti Cave}, the {Juggler} plants a single blade of *grass*, and the yetis declare a **festival**. They hang lanterns, play icicle flutes and dance round the grass in party hats. It is the Grass **Festival**, the biggest night of the yeti year, and the juggler is crowned its king.

In the {Basement} of the {Pool}, the {Tailor} measures a mountain of *soil* for a suit. He sews pockets of **earth**, buttons of pebbles and a worm for a tie. The suit stands up and strolls off, leaving a trail of **earth** across the tiles, and the cleaners chase it with a vacuum.

The {Tailor} stands on the {Staircase} of the {Boathouse}, and a *helping hand* passes him a *war club*. He **throws** it like a boomerang: it knocks over three oars and a pigeon's hat, then whizzes back. He **throws** it again, harder, and this time it comes back holding a fish.

In the {Basement} of the {Boathouse}, the {Magician} pulls a *plum* out of his hat and says it belongs to **a certain** someone. Who? He won't say. **A certain** someone with a beard. A certain someone who rows. Every rower in the boathouse blushes and claims the plum.

The {Ghost} floats up through the {Trapdoor} of the {Mansion} with a magnifying glass to solve a **case**: who stole the *tree* from the garden? The clues lead to the attic, where the tree is hiding in a *safe home* with a teddy bear. **Case** closed, says the ghost, and tucks the tree in with a hot-water bottle.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Lake}'s old pump house, the {Hunter} pokes the chimney, and a cloud of *soot* explodes all over him. He is **black** from boots to hat. The swans scream, thinking he is a giant **black** swan, and he spends the whole afternoon trying to explain.

On the {Staircase} down to the {Lake}, the {Wizard} watches a *sparrow* **maintain** an old wooden bridge with nothing but *silk thread*: stitching cracks, tying loose planks, darning holes. Every morning it **maintains** the bridge again, and every evening the wizard trips over it anyway.

On the {Staircase} of his {Hut}, the {Gardener} beats a strip of *rawhide* until it turns into soft **leather**. He makes **leather** boots, a leather hat and tiny leather jackets for his carrots. The carrots complain that they are too hot, so he gives them leather sunglasses as well.

The {Hunter} rises through a {Trapdoor} in the {Water Park} with a *halberd* and a *standing knife*, and scratches a **plan** onto the slide: here the ambush, there the escape. The ducks gather to admire his **plan**, then switch on the wave machine, and the plan floats away.

On the {Staircase} down to the {Beach}, the {Dentist} meets his greatest **enemy**: a giant toffee with a sticky *tongue*. It licks his *cane* and glues it to the steps. He tugs, it pulls, and they wrestle all the way down to the sand. His **enemy** wins, and the dentist limps off with one boot stuck in toffee.

The {Jockey} taps the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} with his *cane*, and an *arrow landing* on the lid **causes** a chain reaction: the lid flips, honey splashes, a bear sneezes, a tree falls, and a cow ends up on the moon. The bees ask what **caused** it, and everybody points at the jockey.

The {Chef} climbs the {Staircase} of the {Funfair} up a grassy *hillside* facing *east*, and **displays** every cake she has ever baked on its steps. As the sun rises in the east, the icing gleams. Visitors gasp at the **display**, and a seagull swoops off with the top tier.

The {Lifeguard} pops out of a {Trapdoor} in the {Museum} and follows muddy *footsteps* to a statue writing a new **law** with a giant *writing brush*: No running in the museum! She blows her whistle and adds a **law** of her own: no diving off the dinosaurs.

On the {Staircase} into the {Pool}, the {Zookeeper} treads on a giant *foot*. It wiggles its toes. The **foot** belongs to an elephant trying to dip one **foot** into the water, very slowly, because it is cold. The zookeeper gives it a gentle push, and the whole pool sloshes out into the street.

The {Tailor} opens a {Trapdoor} on the {Island}, and a *giant* with a tiny *heart* stomps out, sulking and kicking coconuts. What an **attitude**! The tailor sews him a waistcoat with a heart-shaped pocket. The giant admires himself in a puddle, and his whole **attitude** changes: he starts handing out coconuts.

The {Hunter} stands guard at the {Trapdoor} of the {Pool} with a *door* for a shield, while a *helping hand* **protects** a nervous goldfish in a jar. Seagulls dive-bomb, pelicans swoop. The hunter swings the door, **protecting** the fish from every beak, and the goldfish sleeps through it all.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Beach}'s ice-cream kiosk, the {Cheerleader} twists her body into a *bent cross* and shouts **seven**! Seven seagulls land on her arms. She twists again: seven crabs, seven kites, seven ice creams. In the end she is holding **seven** of everything and cannot move.

The {Shepherd} pops up through the {Trapdoor} of the {Boxing Ring} into a surprise *party* for his sheep. The boxers lose all **interest** in fighting and join in: musical chairs, pin the tail on the ram. Even the referee loses **interest** in the rules and dances the conga with a lamb.

The {Pirate} opens a {Trapdoor} on the {Island}, and *water drops* gush out and split into streams that run off in different directions. Each stream is a **group** with its own idea: one heads for the sea, one for the cave, one for the pirate's boots. He tries to herd every **group** into his hat and ends up soaked.

On the stone {Staircase} of the {Island} temple, the {Hunter} meets a *child* riding a *wild boar* like a pony. The **child** shrieks with joy, bounces down the steps and snatches his hat. The hunter chases them round the island, then gives up, because nobody can catch a **child** on a boar.

The {Yogi} pops up through the {Trapdoor} of the {Mansion} into a grand *assembly* of scientists **testing** a *horse*. Can it count? Can it knit? Can it do the splits? The horse passes every **test**, then turns round and **tests** the yogi, who falls over in his own pose.

On the {Staircase} of his {Hut}, the {Zookeeper} is ambushed by a *debt collector* waving a clipboard. It is your **duty** to feed the penguins! he shouts. It is your **duty** to brush the lions! The zookeeper, guilty, sprints off to do every duty at once, with the collector ticking boxes behind him.

On the {Staircase} into the {Boxing Ring}, the {Yogi} rolls out a carpet of *grass* and pitches a tent. Soon every boxer is setting up **camp**: sleeping bags in the corners, sausages on the ring posts, campfire songs at midnight. The referee joins the **camp** too, in pyjamas and a bow tie.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Boxing Ring}, the {Shepherd} catches a falling *star* in his crook. It is hot, so he juggles it, and it sprinkles glitter over his sheep. They glow all night, the crowd below thinks they are **stars**, and the shepherd's flock becomes the brightest **star** act in town.

The {Gardener} opens the {Trapdoor} of the {Boathouse} and finds a *quotation* written in moonlight above the water, under *many moons* hanging so low the boats glow. He picks one moon, then another, then another, then shouts **enough**! One moon is **enough** for anyone, and the rest float politely away.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Hangar}, the {Jockey} pins a shiny *badge* on each finished **chapter** of his memoir: The Horse Who Flew, The Saddle Disaster. Every **chapter** is folded into a paper plane, and he launches them one by one, until the whole city is reading his life story off their windscreens.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Inn}, the {Yogi} hums, and *music* pours out of his ears like smoke. Every **sound** turns into a colour: a blue cello, a pink trumpet, a lime-green kazoo. Guests lean out of their windows to catch the **sounds** in jam jars and sell them at breakfast.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Funfair}'s ghost train, the {Gardener} finds a *kicking foot* that **follows** her everywhere. She gives it a fierce *glare*, but it keeps **following**, hopping behind her down the ladder, through the dodgems and onto the carousel, nipping at her heels the whole way.

The {Jockey} lifts the {Trapdoor} of the {Beehive} and finds a tiny *scholar* bee with a huge *heart* and an even bigger **ambition**: to fly to the moon. It builds a rocket out of honeycomb. Everyone laughs, but the bee's **ambition** carries it up, up, past the clouds, waving a tiny flag.

In the {Basement} of a *shed* on the {Beach}, the {Dentist} digs through the *foundation*, looking for a lost tooth. Down, down, past crabs and pirate gold, to the **bottom** of the world, where an upside-down sea sloshes. At the very **bottom** he finds his tooth, resting on a velvet cushion.

The {Jockey} rises through the {Trapdoor} of the {Mansion} onto a *podium*, where a *fortune teller* tells him he must **stand** perfectly still for a hundred years to win a prize. He **stands**. Guests hang coats on him, pigeons nest in his cap. He keeps standing, and the prize turns out to be a chair.

On the {Staircase} of the {Mansion}, the {Yogi} meets a **stern** judge with a frown as steep as a *cliff*, who only ever hands out a *silver medal*, never gold. You blinked, she says. You breathed. Even the yogi's beard gets a **stern** look, and the medal seems to glare at him too.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Spa}, the {Baker} watches a *python* gaze down at the hot tubs, **longing for** a warm soak. It sighs, it drools, it writes poems about bubbles. At last the baker lowers it in on a rope, and the moment it is wet, it **longs for** a towel.

The {Lifeguard} pops out of a {Trapdoor} on the {Beach} and pulls a *standing person* out of the *lineup* of swimmers. Here is an **example** of how not to swim! she announces, as he flaps like a chicken. Then she shows a good **example**: a seal, who swims beautifully and gets a medal.

The {Firefighter} sprints up the {Staircase} of the {Hangar} and builds a fort on a *hillside*: a perfect *square* of sandbags. She **defends** it against water balloons, flying custard and a squadron of pigeons. She **defends** it so well that the pigeons surrender and ask to join her side.

On the {Staircase} of the {Pool}, the {Zookeeper} meets a *clan* of penguins, each holding a passport that shows its **nationality**: Emperor, King, Rockhopper. They squabble over which **nationality** gets the best diving board, and the zookeeper settles it by throwing a fish into the deep end.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Lagoon}'s snack bar, the {Gardener} and a *standing person* form a chain of *joined hands* down to the water. Bucket by bucket, they **supply** the fish with lemonade and the turtles with crisps. Soon every creature wants more, and the **supply** runs dry by teatime.

The {Shepherd} rises through a {Trapdoor} in the {Cat Café}, sits with *crossed legs* and taps a sleeping cat with a magic *cane*. The **effect** is instant: the cat sprouts wings and circles the lampshade. He taps another, and the **effect** spreads, until every cat in the café is hovering and purring like a little helicopter.

The {Shepherd} opens a {Trapdoor} in the {Museum} and finds a *market stall* selling one endless *silk thread*. He pulls, and it **continues**: through the Egyptian room, past the dinosaurs, out of the door. Closing time comes, but the thread **continues**, so he keeps pulling all night and by morning has knitted a sock the size of a tent.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Beehive}, the {Sheriff} gives a *snake* orders to **carry out**: slither round the *square*, salute, catch the wasp. The snake **carries out** every order perfectly, then carries out one of its own: it swallows the sheriff's hat whole and wears it as a lump.

The {Lifeguard} tries to leave down the {Staircase} of the {Youth Hostel}, but every backpacker presses a *keepsake* into her hands: a shell, a badge, a slightly chewed postcard. Please **stay**! they beg. Her arms are so full she cannot open the door, so she **stays** another week, then another year.

In the {Basement} of the {Stadium}, the {Juggler} peers into a deep *well*, where a *small speech bubble* **explains** the offside rule. It **explains** it again, more slowly. It draws diagrams on the walls with chalk. By midnight the juggler finally understands, but the bubble has talked itself into a deep sleep.

On the {Staircase} of the {Boxing Ring}, the {Shepherd} sits each sheep in a pair of wooden *stocks*, like a photo booth, and presses its face into wet *soil* to make a mould. Each mould is a **type**: curly, fluffy, grumpy, sleepy. He labels them all, and the boxers queue to find out which **type** of sheep they are.

The {Lifeguard} drops through the {Trapdoor} of the {Cat Café} with a giant *dipper* and scoops *rice* into a heap on the floor. It is building **material**: she glues the grains into bricks and builds a cat castle. The cats bring more **material**, yarn, feathers and a tin of tuna, and the castle grows a fishy tower.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Lagoon}'s ferry office, the {Jockey} knits a *winter coat* from one *silk thread*, row after row, until at last he reaches the **end**. He ties it off. The coat is a hundred metres long and wraps round the whole lagoon. That is the **end** of the thread, and the end of the jockey's patience.

On the {Staircase} of the {Spa}, the {Dentist} finds a *bamboo* basket with a *fitted lid* that **answers** any question. Is flossing fun? Yes. Will it rain? Maybe. What is for dinner? Dumplings. Then he asks how to open it, and the basket **answers** by blowing a loud raspberry.

In the {Basement} of the {Inn}, the {Juggler} winds a *silk skein* round a barrel, round and round, pulling it **tight**. Then **tighter**. The barrel squeaks, the hoops creak, and the cork pops out like a cannonball. By now he has wound himself in so **tight** that he can only hop back upstairs.

On a rickety {Staircase} in the {Swamp}, the {Hunter} trips and smashes a giant egg, and a flood of *yolk* pours down the steps. Everything turns **yellow**: frogs, lily pads, a startled crocodile. He climbs out **yellow** from head to toe, and a line of ducklings decides he is their mother.

On the {Staircase} into the {Ice Rink}, the {Juggler} finds a *rainbow* dangling by a single *silk thread*. Snip! He **cuts off** the thread, and the rainbow falls, shattering into coloured ice cubes. The skaters slide about on them, and the furious rink manager **cuts off** the juggler's free skating for life.

On the {Staircase} down to the {Beach}, the {Cheerleader} meets an *oddball* in a tuxedo made of seaweed, walking a lobster on a lead. How **strange**! He bows, offers her a sand sandwich and sings a love song to a jellyfish. Then it gets even **stranger**: the jellyfish sings back.

On the {Staircase} of the {Spa}, the {Chef} is stopped by a *detective* who **examines** her soup with a magnifying glass. He sniffs it, **examines** a noodle under a microscope, and interviews a carrot. Verdict: too much salt. The chef throws a cucumber slice at him, which he also examines, very carefully.

In the {Basement} of the {Pool}, the {Magician} finds his *mother* knitting swimsuits for everyone. Wear a vest! she shouts, stuffing him into one. Like every **mother**, she has a towel, a snack and a plaster ready. When he pulls a rabbit from his hat, she knits it a jumper too, because she is everybody's **mother**.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Boxing Ring}, the {Juggler} builds a *palace* out of juggling pins and declares it the **capital** of Juggleland. Pigeons queue for passports, and clowns open embassies. Before long the boxers below demand that the **capital** move into the ring, and start fighting over it.

The {Dentist} opens a {Trapdoor} beside the {Swan Pond}, and a *blacksmith* climbs out and hammers a long iron bar into neat **sections**. Clang! One **section** for the bridge, one for the fence, one for the swans' new railings. The dentist takes the last section home as a giant toothpick.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Beach}'s surf school, the {Yogi} balances on one toe, **depending on** a *standing person* to hold the hem of his *robe*. If the person lets go, he falls. The person sneezes, the yogi wobbles, and the surfers below realise they all **depend on** that sneeze never happening again.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Beach}'s pier, the {Pirate} sits with a giant rubber stamp while *twins* bring him plans: a sandcastle, a tunnel to the other side of the world. A *helping hand* stamps every one. He **approves** the castle, **approves** the tunnel, and accidentally **approves** the twins' plan to make him walk the plank.

On a sandy {Staircase} in the {Dunes}, the {Cheerleader} sees a *lord* in a velvet cape leading a huge **crowd** of *sheep* to a picnic. Thousands of them, baaing in chorus. She leads them in a cheer, and the whole **crowd** spells LORD with their woolly bodies, then wanders over to eat his cape.

The {Shepherd} pops through a {Trapdoor} in the {Stadium} with a *workbench* and a *page* listing every **item** he needs for the match: a whistle, a flag, ten thousand hot dogs. He ticks off each **item** as a sheep trots up with it, until the final item, the trophy, arrives in the mouth of a very proud lamb.

The {Gardener} opens a {Trapdoor} in the {Pool}, and a dripping *storyteller* climbs out to explain the **reason** the water is green: a frog prince, a lost slipper, a broken spell. Every time someone asks why, he invents another **reason**, until the swimmers forget the question and just float there, listening.

The {Ghost} hovers over the {Trapdoor} of the {Mansion} as a *helping hand* **presses** a big red button marked *safe home*. Ding! The whole mansion folds itself up like a tent. The ghost **presses** it again, and the mansion springs back up, but upside down, with the butler standing on the ceiling.

On the {Staircase} of his {Hut}, the {Hunter} spills a cup, and the *water drops* will not stop: they trickle, gush and become a roaring **river** down the steps. A fisherman floats past on a log, his *nodding head* bobbing hello. The hunter grabs a paddle and rows his whole hut down the **river** to the sea.

In a {Basement} under the {Beach}, the {Magician} waves his wand at a single grain of *rice*, and it multiplies: ten, a thousand, a million. Soon the basement is packed with **rice**, spraying out onto the sand like a fountain. Seagulls open a sushi bar, and the magician sits on a dune of **rice**, eating with chopsticks.

On the {Staircase} down to the {Lake}, the {Wizard} builds a *fence* and buckles each post with a *leather strap*. It grows and grows until it **surrounds** the whole lake. The ducks are **surrounded**, the fish are surrounded, and a swan files a formal complaint about being fenced in.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Stadium}, the {Juggler} bangs on a *workbench*, and *water drops* start running along the gutter, then pour into a great **river** that wraps round the stadium like a moat. The crowd paddles home in rubber dinghies, and the juggler juggles fish above the **river** for tips.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Beehive}, the {Jockey} watches a *lone bird* **weave** a nest from *silk thread*, in and out, faster than a sewing machine. It **weaves** a nest, then a hammock, then a tiny saddle for the jockey's horse. The bees grow jealous and start weaving tiny scarves of their own.

The {Hunter} opens a {Trapdoor} on the {Island}, and a *pest* scurries out: a tiny beetle that **harms** everything it touches. It nibbles the palm trees, chews the hammock and bites holes in the boat. The hunter chases it with a net, but it **harms** the net too, and he ends up stranded while the beetle sunbathes in his hat.

The {Dentist} bursts through the {Trapdoor} of the {Boathouse} waving a *dipper*, ready to **fight** a rower armed with a soup ladle. Clang! Bonk! They duel across the boats, splashing soup everywhere. The ducks place bets, and the **fight** ends only when both slip into the river and share what is left of the soup.

On the {Rooftop} of the sheriff's office in the {Swamp}, the {Sheriff} holds up *both hands*: in each is a boot, a perfect **pair**. A frog steals one. So he grabs a **pair** of frogs instead, then a pair of crocodiles, and soon he is juggling pairs of everything, with both hands full.

The {Juggler} pops through the {Trapdoor} into the {Boxing Ring} for his grand *finale*, but the **surroundings** have changed overnight: *soil* everywhere, sunflowers tied to the ropes, cows in the front row. He juggles anyway, and his new **surroundings** cheer him on with a chorus of moos.

The {King} opens the {Trapdoor} of a humble {Hut}, and a *guest* climbs in, then another, then a hundred **guests**, all expecting dinner. He gives up his throne, his crown and his slippers. The last **guest** takes his bed, and the king spends the night curled up in the bath.

The {Juggler} opens a {Trapdoor} on the {Beach} and hauls up a *coiled rope* with a *silk thread* tied to every knot. Each knot is an **era**: dinosaurs, pyramids, knights, the invention of ice cream. He unwinds it along the sand, and each **era** comes to life, until a dinosaur is queuing at the ice-cream van.

In the {Basement} of the {Island}'s palace, the {Tsar} meets a *fruit picker* who **picks** everything in sight: mangoes off the ceiling, coconuts off the walls, buttons off the tsar's coat. She **picks** his pocket too, finds a banana, and pops it in her basket with a satisfied nod.

In the {Basement} of the {Museum}, the {Juggler} is at a *party* for the statues when he decides to **lift** the heaviest guest, a marble lion. He bends, heaves, and **lifts** it high over his head. The statues cheer, and the lion, delighted, **lifts** the juggler in return and parades him round the room.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Spa}, the {Sheriff} catches an *assassin* in a dressing gown, armed with a fly swatter. His secret mission: to **kill** every mosquito in the spa. Swat! Swat! He **kills** them all, and the guests sleep soundly for the first time in years, so the sheriff gives him a medal instead of handcuffs.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Lagoon}'s lifeboat shed, the {Gardener} is **attacked** by a seagull. She grabs her *cane*, leaps onto a *workbench* and **attacks** back, swinging wildly. The seagull calls its friends, and soon five hundred birds are on the attack, until she surrenders her sandwich.

The {Firefighter} opens a {Trapdoor} in the {Pool}, and her *father* bursts out in a stripy swimsuit, doing a cannonball. Like any **father**, he tells terrible jokes, soaks the lifeguard and asks if anyone wants a sandwich. Everybody groans, but every other **father** in the pool joins him for one more cannonball.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Pool}, the {Sailor} builds a *workshop* among the *grass* and grows giant **basil**. The leaves are as big as surfboards and smell so strong that swimmers float up the ladder, sniffing. He blends a pesto pool, and everyone swims in **basil**.

The {Magician} slips through a {Trapdoor} on the {Beach} into a *hideout* under a straw *roof*, where he keeps his **secret**: how the rabbit gets into the hat. He tells no one. A crab peeks in, sees the **secret**, and faints. Ever since, every crab on the beach walks sideways, too stunned to walk straight.

On the {Rooftop} of a changing hut on the {Beach}, the {Dentist} meets a *standing person* who keeps sinking into the sand, down past the *foundation*, **lower** and lower, until only his hat shows, very **low** indeed. The dentist lies flat on his tummy to check his teeth, the **lowest** check-up he has ever done.

On the {Staircase} of the {Tower}, the {Chef} carries a cake up to the *royal court*, where lords bow and trumpets blare. The whole **court** falls silent as she lifts the lid. Inside is a tiny dancing king, and the **court** bows to the cake instead of the throne.

In the {Basement} of the {Boathouse}, the {Yogi} meets his new best *friend*: a walrus who also does yoga. They stretch together, meditate together, and get stuck in the same pretzel pose. Rowers try to untangle them, but a **friend** in a knot is still a **friend**, so they stay that way all summer.

The {Sailor} opens a {Trapdoor} in the {Pool}, and a *small speech bubble* floats up carrying a *chipped axe*. It **tells** the axe's story: it chopped an iceberg as big as a whale, lost a chip, and swore revenge. The sailor listens, then **tells** his own story back, and they both weep into the water.

In the {Basement} of the {Beehive}, the {Jockey} holds up a *stop sign*, and every bee **stops** dead in mid-air, buzzing on the spot like a little helicopter. The honey **stops** dripping and the clock **stops** ticking. Then he flips the sign, and they all zoom off at once, straight into his face.

The {Shepherd} opens a {Trapdoor} on the {Beach} and leads his sheep along a *silk thread* stretched over a flooded *rice field*. The thread is so **thin** that only skinny sheep can balance on it. The fluffy ones wobble and splash, so he shears them all, until the flock is as **thin** as noodles.

The {Yogi} opens a {Trapdoor} in the {Mint} and finds a *cliff spring* bubbling with coins. He throws one in, hand on his *heart*, and makes a **wish**: more coins. The spring gushes, and coins spray all over the mint. Now everybody wants a **wish**, and the queue goes round the block.

On the {Rooftop} of the {Yen Exchange}, the {Cheerleader} coaches a squad of a *thousand ants*, waving pom-poms the size of crumbs. One **thousand** tiny voices chant, and they climb into an ant pyramid that spells out a **thousand** in the air. The bankers below gasp and drop a thousand pens.

On the waxy {Staircase} of the {Beehive}, the {Jockey} meets a *standing person* dangling a *plumb line* over every honeycomb to see what it is **worth**. Straight comb: a gold coin. Wonky comb: a button. Then he dangles it over the jockey, frowns, and declares him **worth** exactly three jars of honey.
